goal: Produce a current, holistic, source-bound map of Arcanum's structural governance: constitutions, disciplines, definitions, schemas, validators, lifecycle and promotion processes, registry/generation/runtime projections, observability and maintenance loops, their precedence and integration with the previously mapped Arcanum building protocol, and any structural capability the operator omitted.
context: The study is about public Arcanum as the building system. It must separate canonical meaning, modular law, recurring practice, executable enforcement, capability lifecycle, runtime availability, and non-authority read models. Private DomainSpec and cyberAlchemy-v2 sources may be used only as explicitly labelled comparators or upstream owner evidence and must not be copied into public Arcanum. Inventory is discovery only. The result may diagnose duplication, drift, bugs, and missing owner links, but it authorizes no canonical edit, promotion, publication, deployment, release, or production claim.
anti_bias_global: structural coherence versus owner sovereignty and executable enforcement

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 performs formal and source-archaeological extraction of constitutions and axioms while agent 1 maps disciplines as historical and operational practices on the methodology and source-corpus axes; agent 1 exposes prose-law that lacks a recurring operating practice, while agent 0 exposes practice cards that silently claim constitutional force.

Agent 0 maps normative law and composition while agent 2 traces validators, lifecycle, promotion, registry, generation, installation, runtime parity, and observability on the methodology and source-corpus axes; agent 2 exposes unenforced law, while agent 0 exposes executable checks that outrun their semantic owner.

Agent 1 maps recurring disciplines and their growth or retirement rules while agent 2 maps executable lifecycle and projection machinery on the methodology and source-corpus axes; agent 2 exposes practices with no operational witness, while agent 1 exposes machinery that has become process without an owned discipline.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 attacks duplicate ownership and missed precedent while agent 1 attacks vacuous governance without a finite enforcement witness on the attack-vector axis; each exposes the other's tendency to accept either established prose or executable behavior as sufficient alone.

Agent 0 attacks placement outside an existing owner while agent 2 attacks definitional and authority collapse on the attack-vector axis; a correctly placed rule can still be semantically collapsed, while a precise definition can still duplicate an existing owner.

Agent 1 demands discriminating pass/fail traces while agent 2 demands stable category boundaries on the attack-vector axis; executable behavior without category soundness and clean vocabulary without operational consequence both fail.
